Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt

Class Json

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt.Json
public final class Json extends Object
JSON in and out, with no third-party library.

This is the format every host needs: a Web Browser page hands a script a JSON message, an Espresso panel persists its settings as JSON, and a desktop app talks to a local service over HTTP with a JSON body. RFC 8259 is a small language, so the reader is a hundred lines of direct descent rather than a dependency, and it stays strict on purpose — no comments, no trailing commas, no NaN — because a document that two parsers disagree about is a bug nobody can find later.

The mapping to Mandela values is the obvious one and the one a Java or Kotlin host expects: null, Bool, Int (a long), Double (a double), Str, list, map. Nothing is wrapped, so a decoded document can be indexed and walked with the same syntax as one the script built itself.

Both directions are bounded. Nesting is capped at MAX_DEPTH so a hostile document cannot overflow the Java stack, and the writer refuses values JSON cannot hold — a function, an instance of a script class — rather than inventing a rendering that the reader could not restore. Use stringify(java.lang.Object) when the point is a log line instead of a wire format.

    • stringify

      public static String stringify(Object value)
      Writes a value as text, rendering whatever JSON cannot hold the way println would.

      This is the debugging form: a script printing a map that happens to hold a function or a class instance gets a readable line rather than an error, and the shape stays the same as encode(java.lang.Object) for everything JSON can carry.

      Parameters:
      value - anything
      Returns:
      the text
